title: Batching Scout: continuous workload fingerprinting and safe rollout for batching configs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal:
Build "Batching Scout", a recommendation engine that continuously fingerprints request workloads and proposes safe, reversible batching + caching configs. Deliverables: (1) workload profiler that emits stable fingerprints per route and per-customer; (2) heuristic scoring that balances P95 latency, cost-per-token, and KV cache hit regression; (3) a safe apply/rollback flow (canary, monitor, auto-rollback) that integrates with the console rollout UI and runtime agent.

Background and motivation:
We see significant unit-cost variance across routes due to different sequence-length distributions, arrival processes (Poisson vs bursty), and KV cache utility. Manual batching rules are brittle and rarely updated. Batching Scout should automate configuration suggestions and make applying them low-risk.

Design summary:
- Workload fingerprinting: per-route daily histograms for input token length, prefix reuse rate (KV cache candidate metric), inter-arrival time distribution, and request priority tag breakdown. Fingerprints are compact vectors (stable hash) to allow delta detection.
- Heuristics and scoring: compute expected throughput curve under different "target_batch_size" and "max_latency_ms" pairs using sampled traces and a micro-simulator. Score candidate configs by expected cost reduction vs predicted P95 regression. Apply penalty if KV cache hit-rate drops > 3pp.
- Continuous batching parameters: target_batch_size, batch_timeout_ms, dynamic_batch_multiplier (for bursts), and kv_prefetch_window. Parameters are suggested per-route and can be grouped into policy templates.
- Safe apply/rollback: two-step pipeline — (A) Dry-run simulation using recent replay traces to estimate risk; (B) Canary apply to a weighted traffic slice with automated SLO checks (latency, error-rate, cache-hit). If any SLO threshold breaches, system triggers automated rollback and posts a detailed regression artifact.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Profiler produces per-route fingerprints and shows stable deltas for known workload shifts (test using synthetic shifts).
2) Recommendation engine returns ranked candidate configs with cost/latency delta estimates and confidence score.
3) Dry-run simulator reproduces >90% of observed latency delta magnitude in offline replay tests.
4) Canary rollout mechanism integrates with Console rollouts (UI flag + API) and auto-rolls back on SLO breach within 10 minutes.
5) Documentation and runbook for on-call: how to interpret Scout suggestions, abort a rollout, and examine replay artifacts.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We will keep fingerprint vectors lightweight to avoid long-term storage costs; aggregate histograms at 1-hour granularity and compress via quantiles.
- Simulator complexity: initially use a queuing-based approximator rather than full GPU-queue simulation to keep CPU cost low. This biases conservative latency estimates; acceptable for P1.
- KV cache sensitivity: detecting prefix reuse requires sampling of KV keys — avoid storing raw keys; store hashes and TTL sketches to remain privacy-friendly.
- Opt-in per-customer: some enterprise customers must opt-in for Scout to run on their routes due to compliance.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): profiler + storage schema + console visualization prototype. Dry-run CLI that runs on past 7 days of traces.
- Phase 1 (3 weeks): scoring engine + simple simulator + recommendations API. Internal beta with low-volume routes.
- Phase 2 (2 weeks): canary apply plumbing + auto-rollback + integration tests + runbook.
- Phase 3: expand to 25% of routes and run A/B evals measuring cost reduction and regression rate.
